recipes.name: Berry Cornmeal Muffins
ingredients_raw: 1 (8 ounce) container naturally flavored strawberry yogurt

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease 12 muffin cups or use paper liners.
In a large bowl, sift together the flour, cornmeal, sugar, baking powder, and salt. In a separate bowl gently toss strawberries in 1/2 cup of flour mixture.
Whisk yogurt, melted butter, and egg together. Stir the yogurt mixture into the flour mixture; stir just to moisten. Fold in strawberries. Spoon batter into prepared muffin cups.
Bake in preheated oven for 25 minutes, or until a tooth pick inserted into the center of a muffin comes out clean.

raw_recipe.headline: Berry Cornmeal Muffins
raw_recipe.description: Very refreshing, fruity and delicious! These muffins will bring a smile to anyone's day! Share them with someone you love. You may substitute raspberries or blueberries for the strawberries if you wish and feel free to use either naturally flavored strawberry, banana, or vanilla yogurt.

review.reviewBody: These are very very very good, but you must add the dry to the wet instead of wet to dry. Dont add all the dry, just add till mixture is at desired thickness.
I doubled recipe, added 1Tbsp Local Honey (Strawberries were local too!), and made into Bundt cake with a simple powdered sugar frosting ??

I needed a snack for my daughter after her nap and was tired of feedding her the usual grapes and cheerios so I made these in my mini muffin pan (baked for 17 min) and they were perfect for her. I used frozen strawberries and light sour cream since I didn't have yogurt on hand. I also added a tablespoon of ground flax and 1/4 cup of wheat germ to make them more nutritious and she loved them!

Moist, flavorful and easy to make. I used coconut oil instead of butter and I used Cup 4 Cup gluten-free flour. I used plain Greek yogurt flavored with vanilla (love that you can vary the recipe with different yogurt and berries) and raspberries. I only had course cornmeal and I used that. Next time I'll use just regular cornmeal, course was too crunchy. I didn't have any trouble adding the moist ingredients to the dry and then folding in the berries. I think it is important that you coat the berries with the 1/2 cup flour mixture. Added 5 minutes to the baking time. Definitely will make this again.

exactly what I was looking for, I subbed 1/4 of the cornmeal with Millet as I really Like crunch....and added a 1/2 tsp of lemon extract. topped with cornmeal before baking and have to say yum! used blueberry yogurt and blueberries defrosted.
I did make a few changes ,I used lemon yogurt &added fresh blueberries &the jus of 1/2 a lemon & used whole wheat flour they turned out amazing;would definitely make again ,very moist as well!

Delicious. 
I substituted 1/2 c. whole wheat flour for white, used medium grind cornmeal, non-fat peach yogurt (6 oz. plus splash of milk) and frozen mixed berries. I couldn't keep my hands off of them! I did not coat berries with flour mixture as dough was so thick it wasn't neccessary - no problems with berries settling. I also did not thaw, chop or add sugar to the berries. The whole wheat was a wonderful and healthy addition and did not adversely affect texture. Great and simple recipe.
good twist. Better with 1/2 the cornmeal replaced w flour, too gritty otherwise. Used fresh raspberries.

I added 1/4 cup of almond milk to make it easier to spoon into the muffin tin. I substituted dried cranberries for the strawberries. Tried them when they were still warm; a cakey texture. Made them for a friend, if he likes them I'll make them again.

These muffins were moist and delicious! I used only 1 cup of berries (frozen, with a bit of freezer jam mixed in as ours was about to go bad) and also used plain yogurt to cut down on the sweetness. They also cooked in about 15 minutes so make sure to watch them carefully!
I didn’t have enough strawberries so I added black raspberries to make 2 c chopped fruit & it was delicious!
easy, quick and exactly what I hoped for. I used raspberries!
Super wet and dense. Horrible. Will never make this again.

Yummy muffin that I would make again. Ladies I shared them with loved them. No issues with batter being too thick as others have mentioned...maybe they are using 6 oz cups of yogurt thinking it is a full cup? Only change was that I added chunky sugar to the top before baking to give them a fancier bakery type look.
These muffins were just ok..I didn't think they were moist enough. That weren't horrible but not good enough to make again. sorry
These muffins sing out SPRINGTIME! They are light, flavorful and delicious!

I've made these twice, once with frozen berries and once with fresh. You can always find fresh and I would recommend using that so they don't weigh down these fluffy and tasty muffins. So easy and wonderful. Great option for a healthier muffin.
I wish I could give it more stars! Our favorite version is with key lime yogurt and raspberries. The possibilities are endless and always yummy.

So I can't give this an honest rating because I subbed buttermilk for the yogurt and oats for the cornmeal, and apparently used way too many berries as I had more of a blueberry cobbler thing going on in my muffin tins. HOWEVER, the taste was still pretty good. I feel confident that had I followed the instructions more, it would have been a success.

I really enjoyed this recipe! They just got out of the oven and I can't keep my hands off of them. I'm interested to see how they'll keep with the berries as a few people have mentioned that they make them soggy.
